sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry on non-permeabilized 293T cells (L2). Soluble Vγ4+ TCR binding to FLAG-BTNL3/HA-BTNL8-expressing cells was abrogated by anti-FLAG antibody (steric hindrance by the antibody, not the tag itself) (L3). Anti-FLAG antibody inhibited activation of JRT3 Vγ4Vδ1 TCR transductants by FLAG-BTNL3/HA-BTNL8-expressing 293T cells (L4) — again antibody-mediated blockade, confirming the tag is extracellular and the construct is functional.
sites.rationale: All five ledger lines describe the same N-terminal FLAG-BTNL3 construct. BTNL3 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a signal peptide spanning residues 1–17; the mature extracellular domain begins at residue 18 (Q). An N-terminal tag on such a protein must be placed after the signal peptide cleavage site to avoid being cleaved off — there is exactly one extracellular terminus, so insert_after_residue = 17 is the unique solution. Python confirms residue 17 = G (last SP residue) and residue 18 = Q (mature N-terminus), with 220 residues of extracellular space before the TM boundary at 238. The construct drives Vγ4 T-cell activation (L4), confirming functional integrity of the tagged protein. Full-length human FLAG-BTNL3 (N-terminal FLAG) co-expressed with HA-BTNL8 in 293T cells and CRA123 cells; surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG staining of non-permeabilized cells (L2); IP-MS confirmed full-length protein expression (L5). No residue number is stated in any ledger line; BTNL3 has a signal peptide (1–17) and a single extracellular N-terminus, so the junction is uniquely determined as after residue 17 (the last SP residue), placing the tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 18 onward).

sources.claim: (F) Quantitation of effects of anti-FLAG and anti-HA antibodies on the staining of 293T cells expressing FLAG-BTNL3 and HA-BTNL8 with soluble Vγ4 + TCR and anti-His monoclonal antibody (mAb).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) describe the same construct: full-length human FLAG-BTNL3 with an N-terminal FLAG tag, co-expressed with HA-BTNL8. No ledger line states a specific residue number for the FLAG insertion; the position is topology-derived from the signal peptide boundary (1–17) and the single extracellular N-terminus. L3 notes that anti-FLAG antibody abrogates Vγ4 TCR binding by steric hindrance — this reflects antibody occupancy of the tag near the IgV domain, not disruption of folding or trafficking by the tag itself; the construct is functional. No internal loop insertions are reported in the ledger for BTNL3. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
